tagline: The Art Nouveau capital of Europe — a Hanseatic old town, the world's largest market halls (built as Zeppelin sheds), and Baltic beaches.
overview: Riga is the largest city in the Baltics and the world's capital of Art Nouveau — more than 800 buildings in the style crowd Alberta iela and the surrounding streets with faces, flowers and mythological figures in stone.

The old town wears its Hanseatic trading history in gabled houses, the House of the Blackheads' ornate facade, and St. Peter's church spire overlooking the Daugava river. The Central Market occupies five WWI Zeppelin hangars — Europe's largest market — selling smoked fish, berries and everything else.
Speed's 2024 tour streamed from Riga. The city also claims the world's first decorated Christmas tree (1510, by the Blackheads guild) — a record its neighbour Tallinn cheerfully disputes.

funFacts.title: ART NOUVEAU CAPITAL
funFacts.text: About a third of central Riga is Art Nouveau — the world's largest concentration.

funFacts.title: ZEPPELIN MARKET
funFacts.text: The Central Market's five hangars once housed German airships — now filled with food stalls.

funFacts.title: FIRST CHRISTMAS TREE
funFacts.text: Riga's Blackheads guild reportedly decorated the first Christmas tree in 1510.

funFacts.title: THE BLACKHEADS
funFacts.text: The House of the Blackheads — a bachelor merchants' guild — was rebuilt from ruins in 1999.

funFacts.title: HANSA PORT
funFacts.text: Riga was a powerful Hanseatic trading city for centuries.

funFacts.title: THE BALTIC'S BIGGEST
funFacts.text: With ~600,000 people, Riga is the largest city in the Baltic states.

funFacts.title: JURMALA BEACH
funFacts.text: A 33-km white-sand resort strip is 25 minutes away by train.

funFacts.title: CATHEDRAL OF CATS
funFacts.text: Two cat statues on a merchant's roof famously 'moon' the guild house across the street.

funFacts.title: THE FREEDOM MONUMENT
funFacts.text: The 1935 monument bearing three stars survived Soviet rule as Latvia's symbol.

funFacts.title: BALSAM BITTER
funFacts.text: Riga Black Balsam, the herbal liqueur, has been bottled since 1752.
